provenance.note: The scaling plan states ceilings for USER-FACING surfaces (an API endpoint, a page's first useful content, a browser LCP). This harness measures a PostgreSQL transaction through COMMIT. A transaction is a PROPER SUBSET of an endpoint, so an endpoint ceiling is not an objective for it: using one here would widen a narrow result under a broad name. Every profile below therefore carries objective.state = UNDECLARED and names, for the reader, the nearest declared number and the surface it actually governs. Nothing here guesses a number the plan does not state.

frozen_contracts_referenced_not_restated.name: Accounting Budget A
frozen_contracts_referenced_not_restated.note: The ceiling is NOT copied into this file. The harness reads the constant out of that line when a profile inherits it, so there is exactly one place the number lives. No profile inherits it today: see objective.state on P15-LOAD-002.

sample_counts_are_this_harness_own: The warmup and sample counts below are declared BY THIS HARNESS for its own profiles. They are not the Accounting-A contract's counts and must not be read as restating them; that contract declares its own at tests/performance/accounting-budgets.test.ts:69-70.

invalid_measurement_rules.note: A noisy measurement under contention is an INVALID MEASUREMENT — neither PASS nor FAIL. These are the ONLY rules that may produce that verdict, each with a declared bound, and the harness prints which one fired. A bound here may be TIGHTENED; loosening one to turn an INVALID run green is the weakening this lane exists to prevent.

R1_HOST_LOAD.rule: the 1-minute host load average, divided by the CPU count, exceeds the bound at either the start or the end of the measured region

R2_WARMUP_DRIFT.rule: the steady-state median differs from the warmup median by more than the bound, in either direction — the system never settled, so the samples describe a transient

R3_DISPERSION.rule: p99 divided by p50 exceeds the bound — the sample set is dominated by stalls rather than by the operation

R4_FOREIGN_CLUSTER.rule: a PostgreSQL postmaster other than this harness's own is live on the host while the region is measured (another worker's cluster, a shared dev cluster) — the box is not exclusive, so absolute numbers taken on it prove nothing about the target

verdicts.PASS: objective DECLARED, no INVALID rule fired, every invariant held, and the measured metric is within the objective
verdicts.FAIL: an invariant was violated, or the measured metric is outside a DECLARED objective
verdicts.INVALID MEASUREMENT: at least one invalid_measurement_rule fired — neither PASS nor FAIL
verdicts.UNMEASURED-OBJECTIVE: measured and reported, but the objective is UNDECLARED, so there is nothing to compare against. Never PASS.
verdicts.REFUSAL: no verdict at all, non-zero exit: the profile does not exist, zero rows were seeded, or zero samples were measured

parameter_binding: Each statement is bound, in this fixed order, to $1 = worker index, $2 = iteration index, $3 = a fresh uuid, $4 = key A, $5 = key B. Key A and key B come from keys_sql and are chosen so that A < B, which is what makes the lock order deterministic. The harness passes only as many parameters as the statement's highest $n actually uses.

profiles.title: Concurrent settlement race, deterministic lock order
profiles.surface: one PostgreSQL transaction that locks TWO settlement rows with SELECT ... ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE and moves an allocation between them, through COMMIT, on N concurrent connections over the same small row set
profiles.scenario_source: docs/DAFTAR_SCALING_PLAN.md:34 (concurrent POS peak over shared financial rows); the race shape itself follows the project's existing settlement idempotency work (tests/integration/settlement-s6-idempotency.test.ts)

race.deterministic_lock_ordering: both rows are locked by a single SELECT ... WHERE id IN ($4, $5) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE. Every worker therefore takes the lower id first, which is what makes the race contend without deadlocking. No sleep() appears anywhere in this profile: the contention is PostgreSQL's row locks, not a timer.

objective.reason: No document in this repository states an error-rate ceiling or a latency ceiling for concurrent settlement. The profile's INVARIANT is nonetheless binding and is checked on every run: a violation is a FAIL whatever the objective says.
